q4.forgeability: THE RULE the confirmation must check, all of it, on a GetItem by the client's ticket_id: (1) the item exists; (2) item.ticket_type == 'analysis_request' (lambda_function.py:617); (3) item.source starts with 'dashboard_form:' (lambda_function.py:1299, :1344-1345), the only path whose requester.email is server-derived (lambda_function.py:1296; a CREATE body cannot carry the prefix and its requester.email is body-supplied at lambda_function.py:1373); (4) lower(item.requester.email) == owner.principal_id, the session-verified subject (served.py:334; interactive_access.py:87). Clause (4) is the filer match: a staff user cannot name a real ticket filed by another person, because that ticket's requester.email differs from the caller's session email. Clause (3) is what stops a staff user naming a ticket that a svc CREATE stamped with the staff user's email. A ticket_id that fails any clause leaves ticket_confirmed absent, and producer_for returns YCHARTS (resident_worker.py:180 default). The firm equality is NOT in the rule (not read). LIMIT: the client's ticket_id is still forgeable for the OTHER readers of the record ticket_id (resident_worker.py:240, :385; ops/owned_report.py:76; ycharts/research/opal_packager.py:158). The confirmation fixes the producer choice only. The portal sends the ticket id it holds (portal/src/pages/TicketCenter/analysisRequest.ts:384 'ticket_id: input.ticketId,', on the on-disk checkout; see not_read).

recommendation.deciding_fact: A stamps the producer choice onto the accepted record at the one point where the verified owner and the client's ticket_id are both in hand (submission_service.py:109 gives owner; :145 is the accept call), so producer_for keeps reading only the accepted record, as its docstring requires (resident_worker.py:176-177). B makes the resident read live ticket state at choice time (resident_worker.py:751) under a grant the host does not hold (q2 can_read_today no). The prior read rejected A only for the principal-list variant (adding the staff principal to OPAL_PRODUCER_PRINCIPALS). The stamp variant adds no principal, so the CTO's branch 3 ('no human principal is added', CTO_DELL2_PIVOT_FIRST_ACTS_20261013.md:19-21) holds. Both placements need one GetItem on opal-tickets that does not exist today (generate.tf after :120 for A; resident.tf after :87 for B), so the grant is the shared gate, not the placement.
